newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile 11-mo trade deficit balloons to $981 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chile 11-mo trade deficit balloons to $981 mln.

text.p: Chile's trade deficit widened to $981 million in the first 11 months of the year from a $1.3 billion surplus for the same period last year due to booming imports and a fall in commodity prices which hurt exports, said the Central Bank.
Bank figures showed a trade deficit of $248 million last month compared with a surplus of $73.5 million in the same month last year.

"November's trade figure is explained as much by by the growth of imports -- especially of intermediate goods -- as by the fall in export values as the result of lower prices for our products abroad," said the report.
Exports fell 14 percent last month to $1.2 billion, while imports grew 10 percent to $1.4 billion.
Exports were hurt by a sharp fall in copper exports as a result of the slide in world copper prices over the last year.
Falls were also seen in exports of raw wood pulp, down 53 percent, molybdenum, down 48 percent, sawn wood, down 46 percent and bleached wood pulp which dropped 38 percent on November 1995.
The imports were boosted last month by the increase in intermediate goods imports which have risen 19 percent over the last year, said the report.
It said the growth in intermediate goods imports was mainly the result of the rise in oil imports which jumped 236 percent compared with November 1995.
Consumer goods imports grew a moderate 5.5 percent, which "continues the trend of a slowing in growth rates which has been seen in recent months," it said.
Imports of capital goods fell 2.4 percent last month against November 1995.
